The major components of a typical computer: case/system unit, motherboard, CPU, RAM, storage, power supply, graphics (GPU), cooling
How components connect: motherboard sockets/slots, buses, expansion slots (PCIe), and ports for peripherals
That desktops, laptops, tablets, and phones share the same basic parts in different form factors

claims.claim: Hardware is the material, physical components of a computer system, as distinct from the software that runs on it.
Firmware is programs and data stored inside a hardware component, typically in read-only memory, and is distinct from ordinary software.
The motherboard is the main circuit board that connects the other components and provides communication and power among them through sockets, slots, and buses.
A functional desktop computer is built from a short list of core parts: a case, motherboard, CPU, memory (RAM), storage drive, and power supply, plus graphics and cooling.
The power supply unit converts alternating current from the wall outlet into the low-voltage direct current the internal components use.
RAM is fast, volatile memory whose contents are cleared when power is removed, in contrast to non-volatile storage that keeps files when the machine is off.
Modern expansion cards, including discrete graphics cards, connect through PCI Express (PCIe) expansion slots; graphics may instead be integrated with the CPU or motherboard.
Desktops use standardized motherboard form factors such as ATX, micro-ATX, and mini-ITX; laptops, tablets, and phones package the same basic parts more compactly.
Cooling, whether active (fans) or passive (heat sinks), prevents components such as the CPU from overheating.

sourceRecords.title: Hardware — Glossary
sourceRecords.notes: Fetched 2026-08-19. Defines hardware as 'the material physical components of a system' (sourced to CNSSI 4009-2015 / NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5, SP 800-37 Rev.2, SP 800-171r3). Supports the hardware-versus-software distinction. Federal work; definition re-expressed in original wording, not quoted at length.

sourceRecords.title: Firmware — Glossary
sourceRecords.notes: Fetched 2026-08-19. Defines firmware as computer programs and data stored in hardware, typically in ROM/PROM, that cannot be dynamically modified during execution (CNSSI 4009-2015 via RFC 4949). Supports the firmware-between-hardware-and-software point. Original wording used in the lesson.

sourceRecords.title: Internal Computer Hardware — Introduction to Information and Communication Technology
sourceRecords.notes: Fetched 2026-08-19. Describes motherboard as the central board through which components interface, CPU as executing programs (fetch/decode/execute/writeback), RAM as fast-access memory cleared at power-down, power supply converting AC to low-voltage DC (ATX), and storage (HDD/SSD, RAID). Page marked '© Copyright 2017, Will Brady and Jeffrey Elkner'; treated as reference only, no wording reproduced. Supports motherboard, RAM-volatility, PSU, and storage claims.
